sources.label: Waverley Council — Festival of the Winds

blocks.text: Festival of the Winds is Bondi's free, family-friendly kite festival, held on one breezy spring Sunday each September when the sky above the beach fills with dragons, octopuses, rainbow diamonds and kites the size of small cars. Run by Waverley Council on the Bondi foreshore since 1978, with spectacular hand-made display kites from the Australian Kiteflyers Society, it's my favourite day on the Bondi calendar — and if you've never looked up to see a hundred kites dancing over the surf, you're in for something special.

items.label: What
items.value: Festival of the Winds — Bondi's annual kite festival

items.label: When
items.value: A Sunday in September (spring) — check the official date each year

blocks.text: I love that it's such a local story. Festival of the Winds first took flight in 1978, dreamed up by a small group of Sydney kite enthusiasts who reckoned Bondi in spring — with its wide sand and reliable sea breeze — was the perfect stage. That first gathering drew a curious crowd down to the beach, the idea stuck, and it's been part of the Bondi calendar ever since.

Those early enthusiasts helped grow the day into what it is now, with the Australian Kiteflyers Society bringing their giant hand-made display kites back to the sand year after year. What started as a small community gathering has become one of Australia's best-loved kite festivals, pulling big crowds each spring — proof that a good idea and a strong sea breeze can go a very long way.
What to expect on the day

This is far more than people flying kites in a paddock. The Kiteflyers Society puts on displays with giant, jaw-dropping creations alongside nimble stunt kites, while the rest of the foreshore turns into a proper festival. Expect live music and performance, roaming performers, food stalls, and hands-on kite-making workshops where the kids can build something and send it skyward the same afternoon.

items: Professional kite displays from the Australian Kiteflyers Society — the giant show kites are the stars
Kite-making workshops for children and families
Live entertainment, music and roaming performers across the day
Bring your own kite — everyone's welcome to fly on the grass and sand

blocks.text: Bring your own kite and a picnic rug, then stake out a spot on the grass above the beach early. That elevated parkland strip gives you the whole sky as a backdrop and keeps you out of the thickest crowds down on the sand — and it's the best angle for photos.

blocks.title: Come by public transport
blocks.text: Bondi has very limited parking at the best of times, and on festival day surrounding roads and car parks fill fast or close altogether. Do yourself a favour and catch the train to Bondi Junction then a connecting bus, or the bus straight to the beach. Plan your run with the Transport for NSW trip planner.

Festival of the Winds lands on a Sunday in September each year and runs through the middle of the day into the afternoon, but exact dates and times shift year to year — so I always point people to Waverley Council's official festival page to confirm before they set out. It's free to attend, there's no ticket, and it's genuinely one of the most joyful, unpretentious days out in Sydney. Slap on sunscreen, bring a hat and water, and remember that the same wind lifting all those kites has a bite to it near the water, so pack a layer.

Whether you come to fly your own creation, marvel at the giant show kites, or just lie back on the grass with an ice cream and watch the sky, Festival of the Winds is Bondi at its warm, communal best. Mark it on your calendar — and look up.

items.q: When is Festival of the Winds?
items.a: It's held on a Sunday in September each year to welcome spring. The exact date and times change from year to year, so confirm on Waverley Council's official Festival of the Winds page before you go.

items.q: How much does it cost to attend?
items.a: Nothing — Festival of the Winds is completely free and there's no ticket. You just turn up on the Bondi foreshore.
Along the Bondi Beach foreshore and the parkland above the sand. Honestly, once you're near the beach you can't miss it — just follow the kites.

items.q: Can I bring my own kite?
items.a: Absolutely, that's half the fun. Anyone can fly their own kite on the day, and there are kite-making workshops if you'd rather build one when you arrive.

items.q: What's the best way to get there?
items.a: Public transport, without question. Parking around Bondi is limited and roads get busy or close on the day. Take a train to Bondi Junction and a connecting bus, or a bus directly to Bondi Beach, and check the Transport for NSW trip planner for times.
